meta.model: ZENOJAS XGBoost (top-200 classifier, 11 power-transformed features, trained 2005–2020 and frozen)
meta.horizon: Probability that the stock ranks in the top 200 of the NSE universe (workbook label); skill is measured against the next-quarter holding return with a 60-day reporting lag
meta.test_period: 2021-03-31 to 2026-03-31 (21 quarters, time-based hold-out — every quarter after the training cut-off)
meta.live_period: none: all post-2020 quarters are treated alike as out-of-sample
notes: Scores are probabilities from an XGBoost classifier (400 trees, depth 4, learning rate 0.03, subsample 0.8, column sample 0.8, seed 42) trained on quarterly fundamentals and price factors for ~940 NSE-listed stocks, 2005–2020 (39,716 stock-quarters); they are research output, not investment advice.

Portfolio is the 25 highest-scoring names for the 31-Mar-2026 scoring, equal-weighted, held from 29-May-2026 (60-day reporting lag) and rebalanced quarterly; sector constraints are not applied because the data set carries no sector classification.
57 of 942 stocks had at least one missing input for Q4 FY26; missing values were set to zero before the transforms, as in training.

Diagnostics are measured against the true next-quarter holding return over the 21 out-of-sample quarters: test AUC 0.57 for the top-200 of the holding return, mean rank IC 0.096, positive in 19 of 21 quarters. Much of the signal comes from 12-month momentum (TMR) and Alpha.
Feature importance is permutation importance: the drop in test AUC when one feature is shuffled (5 repeats, seed 42), on the 21 out-of-sample quarters.
Backtest returns are quarterly price returns (no dividends, costs or slippage). The universe excludes delisted firms (survivorship bias), so the equal-weight universe line is the fairer yardstick.
Market-cap bands are by rank within the scored universe (top 100 = Large, 101–250 = Mid, rest = Small), using Bloomberg market caps as of 31 Mar 2026.
